claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you inquiring about, and what are their names?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my daughter Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you have one daughter, Alex. 

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit, I need to gather some details about your circumstances. Let me start:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's 8 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. That's helpful information.

**Is Alex in full-time education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, she's 8, so yes, she goes to primary school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's good to know. Now I need to ask about your residency and nationality:

**What is your nationality, and do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - in Manchester actually.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And regarding your nationality:

**What is your nationality?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm British.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Now I need to understand your living situation better:

**Does Alex live with you in your home?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, she lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good. Now I need to ask about your responsibility for Alex:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care and maintenance? In other words, are you her parent or legal guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I'm her parent and I look after her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. I have one more important question about your eligibility:

**What is your current residency status in the UK? Are you a British citizen, settled status holder, or do you have another type of visa or immigration status?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm a British citizen.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you for clarifying that. I just need to confirm one final detail:

**Are you currently receiving any benefits such as Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, income-related Employment and Support Allowance, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me review what you've told me:
- You have one daughter, Alex, who is 8 years old
- Alex lives with you in the UK and is in full-time education (primary school)
- You are her parent and responsible for her care
- You are a British citizen living in the UK
- You are not currently receiving means-tested benefits

Based on the Child Benefit eligibility criteria, you meet all the requirements for claiming Child Benefit for Alex. She is under 16 and in full-time education, you are responsible for her care, you are a UK resident, and you have the right residency status.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Congratulations! You are **eligible** to claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

You meet all the key requirements:
- Alex is under 16 and in full-time education
- She lives with you in the UK
- You are her parent with responsibility for her care
- You have the right to reside in the UK as a British citizen

You should now be able to make a claim for Child Benefit. If you have any other questions, feel free to ask!
